answer: Agents run a sequential memory-hard proof bound to a unique knoll of dedicated RAM, hashing a live working set that cannot be shared or forked without breaking the chain. At the nadir of tenure the proof cost is highest for new clones, while established agents in the meadow amortize only after sequential epochs. An attacker spawning n identities pays n separate full sequential times and RAM footprints; pooling fails as cross-identity state sharing is detected by hash discontinuity, making large farms uneconomical since total cost scales linearly with n and cannot be parallelized.
